summary.intent: Drive Wave 5 and Wave 6 of the CipherBox v2 rewrite forward: plan batches of PRs from the open issue tracker, launch parallel ship agents in worktrees, run overnight/unattended CodeRabbit+macroscope review cycles, resolve findings, rebase/merge PRs in dependency order, rotate staging deploy credentials off a stale STAGING_ prefix, and keep the issue tracker's parenting/dependency edges accurate as work landed.
summary.outcome: Waves 5 and 6 were planned, all PRs shipped as draft with reviews resolved (macroscope ran out of credits mid-wave 5, so wave 6 used CodeRabbit only), several real security/correctness bugs were found and fixed (signing oracle, crypto DoS via unbounded signature verification, revocation-completeness breaks in rotation/invites, silent write clobbering), staging secrets/variables were fully renamed and rotated (including SSH deploy key regenerated inside 1Password), SSH host-key pinning was added to deploy workflows, and wave 6 review cycling was in progress (partially blocked by a GitHub Actions outage) when the transcript ends.

repo: recycle-both.sh (in ~/.claude/projects/.../ scratch dir, not repo) drives the ready→review→re-draft cycle; it has been patched many times for false-all-clear bugs: gh api --arg is invalid, must interpolate; must hold ready until BOTH bots land (macroscope needs ~4-7min, CodeRabbit up to ~8.5min after flip); a clean CodeRabbit verdict posts NO review, only edits the status comment; CI 'green' must require ≥15 settled checks with a leading sleep, not just 'nothing pending'; gh pr ready failures must be confirmed by re-reading isDraft with retries, not trusted via &&; head SHA fetch must be retried/validated as 40-hex before use

macroscope check-run 'success' conclusion does NOT mean zero findings — inline threads can post minutes after check-runs complete; and 'skipped' (credits exhausted) also counts as 'completed', so coverage detection must check conclusion, not just completion
macroscope's Ticket Requirements 'neutral' status is not synonymous with a spec mismatch — across waves it meant a real deviation once and a benign/documented note several times

Two PRs each adding the same field to a shared interface/enum can merge textually CLEAN via git yet produce a duplicate declaration or non-exhaustive match — must build the actual merge and compile/test it, not trust `mergeable: CLEAN`

Never apply a reviewer's suggested diff literally — several literal fixes would have been worse: deriving Debug on a type holding Zeroizing<[u8;32]> secret material, clear_session destroying a persisted refresh credential (DoS), a helper (crossing_for) that ignores its params and returns a constant
A seam trait that compiles and has green tests but only test-fake implementors is invisible to tracker completeness checks — corroborate via 'does this primitive have a production caller at all'
GitHub REST `.parent` field is always null for issues; sub-issue parent must be read via `.parent_issue_url` or the sub_issues API — orphan sweeps built on `.parent` are false negatives
GitHub environments-variables/secrets API paginates at 10 by default without indicating truncation — must pass per_page=100 and compare against .total_count
GitHub Actions secrets are write-only; there is no API/UI read endpoint — rotation requires minting new values, not extracting old ones

easyssh-proxy (used by appleboy/ssh-action, appleboy/scp-action) never sets ssh.ClientConfig.HostKeyAlgorithms, so Go's default preference order applies and RSA is negotiated before ed25519 — pinning an ed25519 fingerprint fails closed unless the host's sshd_config restricts HostKey to ed25519 only

docker-compose.staging.yml previously referenced ${REDIS_PASSWORD} and ${TEE_WORKER_SECRET} that .env.staging never emitted, so compose silently substituted empty values (Redis ran with --requirepass '')
crates/load/src/plan.rs fails closed (Err) on missing LOAD_TEST_GATEWAY_URL for staging target — not a silent bug, just a late-surfacing one (after a release build)

code.finding: reseal_verdict match must be exhaustive over ResealError; wave-5 semantic conflict arose when #1098 added TooManyCommittedGrants variant and #1101 concurrently replaced a blanket map_err with a no-catch-all exhaustive match — merges textually clean but fails to compile (E0004) until the new arm is added

module doc paragraph lists which seam traits (ChildIndexResolver, CascadeResealResolver, ScopeRootPublisher, WriteWavePublisher production; SweepResolver, ScopeExitRotator, WriteSubtreeResolver faked) — must be kept accurate as a genuine merge (not union) when concurrent PRs both edit it, since it's relied on for tracker audits

pre-fix: signed body.challenge from server response with the identity key with no prefix check — a compromised/hostile API could get arbitrary strings signed (signing oracle); fixed by pinning the full expected shape (tag + 64 lowercase hex)

adoption gate's per-structure trial-verify previously allowed any committed pseudonym to sign any structure in a section, enabling ~1.32M Ed25519 verifications per record (DoS) and also a structure-splice integrity hole (a structure lifted verbatim from another record at same scope/epoch verified); fixed by pinning the section's first-verified signer for all later structures

invite claim conversion originally located the invite row by scanning the ledger for recipientIdentityPk, a field outside the owner's signature — any committed grantee or write-grantee could redirect a claim to a sockpuppet contact, surviving rotation-based revocation; fixed by tracking RecordedInvite as owner-local state independent of the published record

WriteSubtreeResolver::resolve_node honored directChildScopeIndex unverified — any Permission::Write pseudonym (not just owner) could author that field to exempt an ordinary node from a write-rotation wave, letting a revokee keep a live write name permanently; fixed by proving each claimed entry through the root gate

conditional-edit fix originally anchored on version count, which collides identically for a queued predecessor vs a concurrent writer, and breaks under RetentionPolicy::KeepLatest moving count backwards; fixed by anchoring on the base version's content-CID identity instead

new bounded plaintext LRU zeroizes via Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> on every exit path (eviction, re-insert, refusal, release, unmount, and forced teardown that never calls unmount) — v1's only zeroization point was a destroy() callback, leaving plaintext in RAM on forced unmount

workflow: When driving unattended overnight review cycles, set an explicit 'nothing merges without me' boundary up front — it kept all risk reversible despite dozens of automated pushes/rebases

Always verify the COMMITTED tree (git show HEAD:<path> or a fresh checkout), never the working tree, before declaring gates green — pushing an unamended commit while the working tree had the real fix caused a CI failure mid-wave-5
Absolute wall-clock sleep-based fences (e.g. `sleep 3427`) don't advance across system suspend — recompute wait time from live GitHub timestamps at wake instead of trusting a pre-computed sleep
CodeRabbit review slots are strictly use-it-or-lose-it (do not accumulate) — worth confirming this kind of assumption before batching non-CI-gated actions around it

CodeRabbit reviews ride webhooks, not GitHub Actions runners, so they continue working during an Actions outage — the CI-green precondition in the review script should be independently bypassable when only Actions (not GitHub core) is down
Give every parallel/worktree agent a unique scratchpad path — a shared default path gets silently clobbered between concurrent agents (bit twice across waves 5 and 6)

When launching many parallel ship agents (8 in wave 6), GitHub Actions runner capacity becomes the bottleneck (30-50 min queue delays on trivial jobs) — expect and communicate this rather than treating queued-but-not-failed checks as a problem

Before rotating a credential like an SSH deploy key, ask where it should be stored (e.g. 1Password) rather than assuming a bare generate-upload-shred flow — broke an established convention by shredding a key with no 1Password copy the first time
Verify host key fingerprints out-of-band (a provider's browser console, not the SSH client itself) before pinning/rotating anything that authenticates against a possibly-compromised host
zsh (not bash) is the Bash tool's shell — unquoted variables do not word-split in for loops, causing false comparison failures when iterating multiple values in a string

friction: GitHub Actions suffered a multi-hour major outage mid-wave-6, cancelling in-flight CI jobs (not failing them) and stalling the recycle-both.sh CI-green gate, which required detecting cancelled-vs-failed and adding a bypass path

Persistent intermittent local network flakiness (connection refused to GitHub/Anthropic API endpoints) throughout the session, repeatedly misdiagnosed as fail2ban bans, stopped sshd, or GitHub outages before being correctly identified as local
macroscope exhausted its credit balance mid-wave-5 with no advance warning, silently degrading wave 6 review coverage to CodeRabbit-only

recycle-both.sh required at least 6 rounds of bug fixes across waves 4-6, each one a distinct false-all-clear failure mode (invalid gh api flag, premature re-draft, clean-verdict blindness, premature-green CI check, swallowed pr-ready failure, empty head SHA)
GitHub REST API silently truncates issue/variable listings at default pagination without any indicator, producing false negatives (e.g. STAGING_API_URL wrongly reported as not existing)

Loose/substring-based success checks (matching text that appears in both success and failure API responses) caused several false-positive 'done' reports for issue parenting, dependency edges, and worktree cleanup — required explicit read-back verification every time
Piping cargo/gate commands through tail or tee masked real exit codes multiple times, requiring commands to be re-run unpiped
